draft:
We saw a person's faith as a building, resting on one foundation stone and rising piece by piece [[syr.dw.doubt]] [[as:paraphrase]].

A building is not finished in a day [[syr.dw.doubt]] [[as:paraphrase]].

What we distrusted was not the struggling believer, but the prying scrutinizer, who would take the Godhead apart like a problem to be solved [[syr.dw.doubt]] [[as:paraphrase]].

Our faith was questioned, and it kept growing [[syr.dw.doubt]] [[as:paraphrase]].

The Persian sage wrote in Demonstration I: [[quote:syr.quote.aphrahat-stone-foundation]]

The believer becomes a dwelling-place for Christ, and a king's dwelling is not left bare [[syr.dw.adam-grace]] [[as:paraphrase]].

For the one who falls, Aphrahat named penitence as the medicine for the wound [[syr.limit.what-must-one-do]] [[as:paraphrase]].

Who is finally counted among the saved, Aphrahat leaves to the judge [[syr.limit.what-must-one-do]] [[as:paraphrase]].
